mainTopic: Sins that bring death to one's family, and other sins with matching punishments and rewards
overview: This amud discusses which sins bring death to a person's wife or young children. רבי נתן says unfulfilled נדרים cause a man's wife to die, and רבי says they cause young children to die. In another ברייתא, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון blames נדרים and רבי יהודה הנשיא blames ביטול תורה. The גמרא explains that רבי changed his mind after hearing רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. More opinions follow: אמוראים argue whether the sin is neglecting מזוזה or ביטול תורה, and תנאים argue whether it is מזוזה or ציצית. Each view is tied to a פסוק. ריש לקיש then praises ציצית: a careful person will be served by 2,800 servants. Next the גמרא gives a סימן and lists sins with matching punishments: שנאת חנם, not separating חלה, and not separating תרומות ומעשרות. For חלה and מעשרות it also promises a reward. The amud ends with גזל, which brings locusts and famine, and רבא begins comparing the 'cows of Bashan' to the women of מחוזא, a comparison that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: These מצוות were entrusted even to unlearned people
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the previous explanation: the מצוות under discussion were handed over to עמי הארץ as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they were handed over to the unlearned people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the explanation it began on the previous amud. It says these מצוות were entrusted even to ordinary, unlearned people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because these מצוות were given to everyone, including עמי הארץ, people who neglect them cannot excuse themselves for not knowing. That is why neglecting them brings punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: unlearned people, people ignorant of Torah

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of a sentence on the previous amud. It is not a new statement on its own, so don't look for a new topic here.

phrases.english: and they were handed over to the unlearned people.
phrases.notes: This wraps up the earlier talk about certain מצוות and why neglecting them is punished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the explanation that began on the earlier part of the דף.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: These מצוות were given to all of Israel, even the unlearned, so neglecting them carries a penalty.

steps.title: רבי נתן: unfulfilled vows can cost a man his wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן teaches that because of the sin of unfulfilled נדרים a man's wife dies, and he brings a פסוק from משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי נתן says, because of the sin of vows a man's wife dies. As it says: "If you have nothing to pay, why should He take your bed out from under you?"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא in which רבי נתן names a punishment for breaking a נדר: the man's wife dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about someone who 'has nothing to pay.' רבי נתן reads this as a person who made a נדר and did not pay it. 'Your bed' (משכבך) is read as a reference to his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא
because of the sin of vows (made and not fulfilled)
your bed; here a hint to one's wife

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Natan says:

phrases.aramaic: בַּעֲוֹן נְדָרִים מֵתָה אִשָּׁה שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: For the sin of vows, a man's wife dies,
as it says: "If you have nothing to pay,
phrases.notes: משלי כב:כז

phrases.english: why should He take your bed from under you?"
phrases.notes: 'Your bed' is read as a hint to one's wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: punishments for unfulfilled נדרים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unfulfilled נדרים can cause the death of one's wife.

steps.title: רבי: unfulfilled vows can cost a man his young children
steps.stepSummary: רבי says unfulfilled נדרים cause young children to die. He learns this from a פסוק in קהלת that speaks of destroying 'the work of your hands,' which he explains as one's children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: for the sin of vows, children die while they are young. As it says: "Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and do not say before the messenger that it was a mistake. Why should God be angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands?" What is the work of a person's hands? You must say: his sons and daughters.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives a different punishment for breaking נדרים: young children die. He proves it from a פסוק and then explains which word in the פסוק points to children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verses in קהלת are about making a נדר and not keeping it. The punishment named is that God will 'destroy the work of your hands.' רבי asks what 'the work of a person's hands' means and answers that it is his children.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, compiler of the משנה
you must say / it must mean

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא. Remember this, because the גמרא will soon use it to ask a question.

phrases.english: Rabbi says:

phrases.aramaic: בַּעֲוֹן נְדָרִים בָּנִים מֵתִים כְּשֶׁהֵן קְטַנִּים,
phrases.english: For the sin of vows, children die when they are young,
as it says: "Do not let your mouth
phrases.notes: קהלת ה:ה

phrases.english: bring your flesh to sin,
and do not say before the messenger
that it was a mistake;
why should God be angry at your voice
and destroy the work of your hands?"

phrases.aramaic: אֵיזֶה הֵן מַעֲשֵׂה יָדָיו שֶׁל אָדָם?
phrases.english: What is the work of a person's hands?

phrases.aramaic: הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר בָּנָיו וּבְנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם.
phrases.english: You must say: a person's sons and daughters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second view on the punishment for unfulfilled נדרים: children instead of a wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unfulfilled נדרים can cause young children to die.

steps.title: A dispute: vows or neglecting Torah study
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a מחלוקת about why children die. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says it is because of נדרים, and רבי יהודה הנשיא says it is because of ביטול תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: for the sin of vows, children die. These are the words of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. רבי יהודה הנשיא says: for the sin of neglecting Torah study.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא in which two תנאים argue about which sin causes children to die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now have two possible causes for the same punishment: breaking נדרים, or ביטול תורה. Notice that רבי יהודה הנשיא is listed here with the ביטול תורה view.

keyTerms.meaning: neglecting / wasting time from Torah study

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
For the sin of vows, children die,
these are the words of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon.
Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says:
for the sin of neglecting Torah study.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא about the death of children, now with a מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: children die because of נדרים. רבי יהודה הנשיא: because of ביטול תורה.

steps.title: What verse supports the ביטול תורה view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that the נדרים view has a source, and asks for the source of the ביטול תורה view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says 'because of vows,' as we said. But for the one who says 'because of neglecting Torah,' what is his verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question to prepare the next step. It wants the פסוק behind רבי יהודה הנשיא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נדרים view already has a source, the פסוק in קהלת quoted in step 3. The ביטול תורה view has not yet been tied to any פסוק, so the גמרא asks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: according to the one who says

phrases.english: It makes sense for the one who says 'for the sin of vows' —
as we said,
phrases.notes: Referring to the פסוק from קהלת in step 3.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בַּעֲוֹן בִּיטּוּל תּוֹרָה
phrases.english: but for the one who says 'for the sin of neglecting Torah,'
what is the verse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the second opinion in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the view that children die because of ביטול תורה.

steps.title: The source: 'In vain I struck your children'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a פסוק from ירמיהו: the children were struck because the people did not accept מוסר, meaning Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "In vain I struck your children; they did not accept instruction."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק that links the death of children to not accepting Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'They did not accept מוסר' is read as the fathers refusing Torah teaching. The children were struck because of that, which is the ביטול תורה view.

keyTerms.meaning: instruction / discipline, here referring to Torah

phrases.english: As it is written: "In vain I struck your children;
phrases.notes: ירמיהו ב:ל

phrases.english: they did not accept instruction."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in ירמיהו connects the children's death to rejecting מוסר, which is Torah.

steps.title: The same verse can also support the vows view
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the נדרים view can also be learned from this פסוק, reading לשוא as 'over matters of emptiness,' meaning empty vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: for the one who says 'for the sin of vows,' it can also be learned from here: "In vain I struck your children" means over matters of emptiness.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק shows that the same פסוק from ירמיהו also works for the נדרים view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads לשוא not as 'for nothing' but as 'because of שוא,' empty matters. A נדר that is made and never kept is empty speech, so the פסוק fits the נדרים view too.

keyTerms.meaning: because of empty matters (empty, unfulfilled words)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
According to the one who says 'for the sin of vows,'
it can also be learned from here:
"In vain I struck your children" —
over matters of emptiness.
phrases.notes: Empty words, meaning vows that were not fulfilled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-reads the same פסוק from step 6 in favor of the other opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לשוא can mean 'because of empty matters,' so the פסוק also supports the נדרים view.

steps.title: Isn't רבי יהודה הנשיא the same as רבי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבי יהודה הנשיא is the same person as רבי, and רבי said children die because of נדרים. How can he also say ביטול תורה?
steps.simpleTranslation: After all, רבי יהודה הנשיא is the same as רבי, and רבי says it is because of vows!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a contradiction between two statements made by the same person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 3, רבי said children die because of נדרים. In step 4, רבי יהודה הנשיא said ביטול תורה. Since these are one and the same person, his two statements seem to contradict each other.

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא הַיְינוּ רַבִּי,
phrases.english: After all, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi is the same as Rabbi,
and Rabbi says it is for the sin of vows?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא הַיְינוּ רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares step 3 with step 4 and finds a contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling attributed to רבי יהודה הנשיא in step 4 (ביטול תורה).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same person cannot hold two different causes; in step 3 רבי said נדרים.

steps.title: He changed his mind after hearing רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי first held ביטול תורה. After he heard רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון say נדרים, he changed his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: That was after he heard it from רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying the two statements come from different times in רבי's life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His original view was ביטול תורה, as recorded in step 4. Once he heard רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view, he accepted it and taught נדרים, as recorded in step 3. So there is no contradiction; he retracted.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying רבי held both views at once. He changed his mind, and his later view is נדרים.

phrases.aramaic: בָּתַר דְּשַׁמְעַהּ מֵרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: After he heard it from Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּתַר דְּשַׁמְעַהּ מֵרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction: the two statements come from different times.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי held two conflicting views about the same punishment.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי first said ביטול תורה, then switched to נדרים after hearing רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

steps.title: A new dispute: מזוזה or ביטול תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא and רבי יוסי argue. One says children die because of neglecting מזוזה, the other says because of ביטול תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא and רבי יוסי disagree about this. One says: for the sin of מזוזה. The other says: for the sin of neglecting Torah study.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new מחלוקת between אמוראים about why children die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new possible cause appears: failing to put up a מזוזה. The other side keeps the ביטול תורה view. The גמרא does not say which אמורא holds which view.

keyTerms.meaning: the scroll placed on the doorpost

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba and Rabbi Yosei disagree about it:
One says: for the sin of mezuzah.
And one says: for the sin of neglecting Torah study.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another מחלוקת on the same question of why children die.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One אמורא says children die because of neglecting מזוזה; the other says because of ביטול תורה.

steps.title: The root of the dispute: how far back a verse connects
steps.stepSummary: The disagreement depends on a rule of דרשה. The מזוזה view connects a פסוק only to the verse right before it. The ביטול תורה view also connects it to the verse before that one.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says 'for the sin of מזוזה': a verse is interpreted with the verse right before it, but not with the verse before that. According to the one who says 'for the sin of neglecting Torah': a verse is interpreted with the verse right before it and also with the verse before that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the two אמוראים disagree. Each one links the same פסוק to a different earlier verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In דברים, the promise 'so that your days and your children's days may be long' (11:21) comes right after the מזוזה verse (11:20). Before that is the verse about teaching Torah to your children (11:19). If a פסוק links only to the verse right before it, the reward is tied to מזוזה. If it can link two verses back, it is also tied to Torah study.

keyTerms.meaning: with the verse right before it
with the verse before the one before it (two verses back)

steps.whatToRemember: Three sins are suggested as causes of children dying: unfulfilled נדרים, ביטול תורה, and neglecting מזוזה. רבי ended up holding נדרים. The מזוזה versus ביטול תורה dispute depends on whether a פסוק can be linked only to the verse right before it, or also to the verse two back.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how one rule about reading verses (לפניו versus לפני פניו) can produce two different practical lessons from the same פסוק.

phrases.english: According to the one who says 'for the sin of mezuzah,'
a verse is interpreted with the one right before it
phrases.notes: דברים יא:כא is read together with the פסוק right before it, יא:כ, about מזוזה.

phrases.english: and not with the one before that.
And according to the one who says 'for the sin of neglecting Torah,'
a verse is interpreted with the one right before it
and also with the one before that.
phrases.notes: Also connected to 11:19, teaching Torah to one's children.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בַּעֲוֹן מְזוּזָה, מִקְרָא נִדְרָשׁ לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the מחלוקת in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מזוזה versus ביטול תורה dispute comes from whether a פסוק is interpreted only with the verse right before it, or also with the verse two back.

steps.title: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue: מזוזה or ציצית
steps.stepSummary: Two תנאים disagree about which sin causes children to die. One says neglecting מזוזה and the other says neglecting ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה also argued about this. One said children die because of the sin of מזוזה. The other said they die because of the sin of ציצית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more disagreement about why young children die. This time it is between two תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just saw אמוראים argue מזוזה versus ביטול תורה. Now earlier authorities argue too, with a new option: ציצית. The גמרא does not say who holds which view. It just says 'one said' and 'one said.'

keyTerms.meaning: One said... and the other said (the speakers are not identified)

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda disagree about this.
phrases.notes: 'This' means the question of why young children die.

phrases.english: One said: because of the sin of mezuza,
and one said: because of the sin of tzitzis.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a disagreement between תנאים on the same topic as the אמוראים in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One תנא blames neglect of מזוזה, the other blames neglect of ציצית.

steps.title: The מזוזה view has a source, but what is the ציצית view's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that the מזוזה view has a clear source. It asks what the source is for the ציצית view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says מזוזה. It is written, 'And you shall write them on the doorposts of your house,' and right after that it says, 'So that your days and the days of your children may be many.' But for the one who says ציצית, what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the source for the מזוזה view. Then it asks for the source of the ציצית view. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the תורה, the מזוזה command is placed right next to a promise of long life for 'your children.' So neglecting מזוזה can cost children their lives. ציצית has no verse like that nearby, so the גמרא asks where that view comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense for... (first half of a 'this side is fine, but that side?' question)

phrases.english: It makes sense according to the one who said: because of the sin of mezuza,
as it is written: 'And you shall write them on the doorposts of your house,'
and it is written after it:
'So that your days may be many, and the days of your children.'
But according to the one who said: because of the sin of tzitzis,
what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the sources behind the two views in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק links neglecting ציצית to children dying?

steps.title: Source for ציצית: 'Also on your corners is found blood'
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא (some say שילא מרי) brings a verse from ירמיה that connects 'corners' (כנפים) with the blood of innocent souls.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said, and some say it was שילא מרי: It is written, 'Also on your corners is found the blood of the souls of the innocent poor.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing a פסוק for the ציצית view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ציצית are tied to the corners (כנפים) of a garment. The verse says blood is found 'on your corners.' The 'innocent' souls are read as young children, who have not had a chance to sin. So neglecting the corners, meaning ציצית, leads to their death.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (the statement may belong to a different speaker)
Your corners / the edges of your garment

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא שֵׁילָא מָרִי,
phrases.english: Rav Kahana said, and some say it was Sheila Mari:
As it is written: 'Also on your corners is found'
'the blood of the souls of the innocent poor.'
phrases.notes: ירמיה ב:לד

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא שֵׁילָא מָרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word כנפים in ירמיה hints at ציצית. The 'innocent souls' are children who die because of this sin.

steps.title: The same verse also supports the מזוזה view
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the next words of the same verse support the מזוזה view: entrances without a מזוזה are like a thief's break-in hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The one who says מזוזה can also learn it from here. It is written, 'You did not find them breaking in.' This means they made their doorways like a break-in hole.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds that the very same verse in ירמיה can also support the מזוזה view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse goes on: 'You did not find them breaking in (במחתרת).' A doorway with no מזוזה is like a hole a thief cuts in a wall. It is just an opening, not a proper Jewish doorway. This mirrors Step 7, where רב נחמן בר יצחק also showed that another view could be read into a verse.

keyTerms.meaning: A break-in hole dug by a thief

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בַּעֲוֹן מְזוּזָה נָמֵי מֵהָכָא,
phrases.english: According to the one who said 'because of the sin of mezuza,' it is also from here,
as it is written: 'You did not find them breaking in' —
meaning that they made doorways like a break-in hole.
phrases.notes: That is, doorways without a מזוזה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the continuation of the same verse from Step 14 in favor of the מזוזה view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Doorways without a מזוזה are like a thief's break-in. The ירמיה verse therefore supports the מזוזה view too.
steps.whatToRemember: Children dying is linked to מזוזה (because of how verses are placed next to each other, and 'like a break-in') or to ציצית ('on your corners').

steps.title: The reward for being careful with ציצית
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches that a person who is careful with ציצית will be served by 2,800 servants. His source is a verse in זכריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Anyone who is careful with ציצית will merit to have 2,800 servants serve him. As it says: 'So says ה׳ of hosts: In those days, ten men from all the languages of the nations will take hold of the corner of a Jewish man's garment, saying: Let us go with you.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since ציצית just came up, the גמרא adds a teaching about the great reward for keeping it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten men from each of the 70 nations take hold of each corner, which makes 700 per corner. Four corners × 700 = 2,800. The punishment for neglecting ציצית is now balanced by the reward for keeping it.

keyTerms.meaning: The corner of a Jewish man's garment

steps.confusionAlert: The number 2,800 is not stated in the verse. It comes from 10 men × 70 languages × 4 corners.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Anyone who is careful with tzitzis merits

phrases.aramaic: וּמְשַׁמְּשִׁין לוֹ שְׁנֵי אֲלָפִים וּשְׁמוֹנֶה מֵאוֹת עֲבָדִים.
phrases.english: that two thousand eight hundred servants will serve him.
As it is said: 'So says ה׳ of hosts: In those days'
'ten men will take hold'
'from all the languages of the nations'
phrases.notes: There are 70 nations, each with its own language.

phrases.english: 'and they will take hold of the corner of a Jewish man's garment,'
'saying: Let us go with you, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כׇּל הַזָּהִיר בְּצִיצִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the mention of ציצית with a teaching about its reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person careful with ציצית merits 2,800 servants.

steps.title: A memory aid for the coming list of sins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן, a list of keywords, to help remember the order of the teachings that come next about sins and their punishments.
steps.simpleTranslation: A memory sign: Hatred, חלה, תרומה, stolen, judgment, oath, spilling, uncovering, and vulgarity.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא gives a list of keywords so we can remember the teachings that are about to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word stands for one coming teaching about a sin and its punishment. This amud covers the first four: hatred (שנאת חנם), חלה, תרומה, and 'stolen' (גזל, which starts in step 27). The other keywords refer to teachings later on the daf.
steps.confusionAlert: A סימן is not a teaching in itself. It is only a list of keywords to help you remember the order of what comes next.

phrases.english: A memory sign:
Hatred, challah, teruma, stolen,
judgment, oath, spilling, uncovering, and vulgarity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from ציצית to a new series of teachings about sins and their punishments.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gives the order of the coming teachings.

steps.title: The punishment for baseless hatred
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה teaches that שנאת חנם brings fighting at home, miscarriages, and the death of young children.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי נחמיה says: Because of the sin of baseless hatred, there is great fighting inside a person's home, his wife has miscarriages, and his sons and daughters die while they are young.
steps.whatsHappening: The first item in the סימן, 'hatred,' is now explained. רבי נחמיה lists the punishments for שנאת חנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The punishment matches the sin. Hatred of others leads to fighting inside one's own home. The death of young children also connects back to the earlier discussion about why children die.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Nechemya says:
Because of the sin of baseless hatred,

phrases.aramaic: מְרִיבָה רָבָה בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: great fighting increases inside a person's home,
and his wife miscarries,

phrases.aramaic: וּבָנָיו וּבְנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם מֵתִים כְּשֶׁהֵן קְטַנִּים.
phrases.english: and a person's sons and daughters die while they are young.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first keyword of the סימן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שנאת חנם brings fighting at home, miscarriages, and the death of young children.

steps.title: The punishment for not separating חלה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי יהודה teaches that not separating חלה brings no blessing on stored grain, high prices, and others eating your crops. He reads a verse with a word change: בחלה instead of בהלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי יהודה says: Because of the sin of חלה, there is no blessing on what is gathered in, a curse spreads to the prices, and people plant seeds and others eat them. As it says: 'I will also do this to you: I will bring terror (בהלה) on you, consumption and fever that wear out the eyes and make the soul ache, and you will plant your seed for nothing, and your enemies will eat it.' Do not read 'בהלה' (terror). Read 'בחלה' (because of חלה).
steps.whatsHappening: The second item of the סימן, 'חלה,' is explained. The proof comes from a verse that is read with one letter changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in ויקרא lists punishments, including 'your enemies will eat' your crops. By reading בהלה as בחלה, the verse now names the sin behind these punishments: neglecting חלה. The punishment fits the sin, since holding back part of the dough leads to losing your grain.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of dough given to a כהן
Do not read it as... but as... (a דרשה that changes how a word is read)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אל תקרי' does not change the text of the פסוק. It adds a second layer of meaning on top of the plain reading.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
Because of the sin of challah, there is no blessing on what is gathered in,
and a curse spreads to the prices,
phrases.notes: שערים here means market prices.

phrases.english: and they plant seeds and others eat them,
as it is said: 'I also will do this to you:'
'I will bring upon you terror,'
'consumption and fever,'
'that wear out the eyes and make the soul ache,'
'and you will plant your seed for nothing, and your enemies will eat it.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא כו:טז

phrases.english: Do not read 'behala' (terror), but 'bechalla' (because of challah).

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בַּעֲוֹן חַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second keyword of the סימן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neglecting חלה brings a lack of blessing, high prices, and enemies eating your crops.

steps.title: Giving חלה brings blessing
steps.stepSummary: The other side: those who give חלה are blessed, as a verse in יחזקאל says.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they give it, they are blessed. As it says: 'And the first of your dough you shall give to the כהן, to bring a blessing to rest on your house.'
steps.whatsHappening: After the punishment, the teaching gives the positive side: the reward for giving חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse calls חלה 'the first of your dough' and directly promises 'a blessing on your house.' This is the reverse of 'no blessing on what is gathered in' from the previous step.

phrases.english: And if they give it, they are blessed,
as it is said: 'And the first of your dough you shall give to the priest,'
'to bring a blessing to rest on your house.'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל מד:ל

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reward side of the חלה teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those who give חלה are blessed.

steps.title: The punishment for neglecting תרומות and מעשרות
steps.stepSummary: Not separating תרומות ומעשרות holds back dew and rain, makes prices high, and leaves people unable to earn a living. A verse in איוב is the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the sin of not separating תרומות and מעשרות, the heavens are held back from bringing dew and rain, prices go up, profit is lost, and people chase their livelihood and cannot reach it. As it says: 'Drought and heat steal the snow waters; the grave takes those who sinned.'
steps.whatsHappening: The third item of the סימן, 'תרומה,' is explained. The teaching lists punishments for not separating תרומות ומעשרות and quotes a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The punishment fits the sin. A person who holds back the gifts from the crops loses the rain that makes crops grow. How the verse in איוב teaches this is not clear yet, and the גמרא will ask about it next.

keyTerms.meaning: Failing to separate the gifts from produce

phrases.english: Because of the sin of neglecting terumos and maasros,
the heavens are held back from bringing down dew and rain,
and high prices come, and profit is lost,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְנֵי אָדָם רָצִין אַחַר פַּרְנָסָתָן וְאֵין מַגִּיעִין,
phrases.english: and people run after their livelihood but do not reach it,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״צִיָּה גַם חוֹם יִגְזְלוּ מֵימֵי שֶׁלֶג
phrases.english: as it is said: 'Drought and heat steal the snow waters;'
'the grave takes those who sinned.'
phrases.notes: איוב כד:יט

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the third keyword of the סימן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neglecting תרומות ומעשרות holds back rain and brings economic hardship.

steps.title: How does the verse show this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the verse in איוב shows that neglecting תרומות ומעשרות causes drought.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning? How do we see this from the verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the verse connects to תרומות ומעשרות. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse talks about drought and stolen snow water, but it never mentions תרומות ומעשרות. The גמרא wants to know where that link comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning / how is this shown?

phrases.english: What is the meaning (how is this shown)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the verse quoted in Step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the איוב verse refers to תרומות ומעשרות.

steps.title: Summer sins take away winter rain
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל explains: the gifts you were commanded to give in the hot season and did not give cause the snow waters to be 'stolen' from you in the rainy season.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Because of the things I commanded you in the hot season and you did not do them, the snow waters will be stolen from you in the rainy season.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining how to read the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ציה גם חום' (drought and heat) is read as the summer, which is harvest time, when תרומות ומעשרות must be separated. 'יגזלו מימי שלג' means that, as a result, the winter rains are taken away. The sin of 'holding back' the gifts is paid back by 'stealing' the rain.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁבִיל דְּבָרִים שֶׁצִּוִּיתִי אֶתְכֶם בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה
phrases.english: Because of things that I commanded you in the hot season,
and you did not do them,

phrases.aramaic: יִגָּזְלוּ מִכֶּם מֵימֵי שֶׁלֶג בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים.
phrases.english: the snow waters will be stolen from you in the rainy season.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The summer heat stands for the harvest season of מעשרות. The stolen snow waters are the winter rain held back as punishment.

steps.title: Giving מעשרות brings an overflowing blessing
steps.stepSummary: Those who give תרומות ומעשרות are blessed. ה׳ promises in מלאכי to open the windows of heaven and pour out blessing 'עד בלי די.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they give, they are blessed. As it says: 'Bring all the מעשר into the storehouse, so that there will be food in My house, and test Me now with this, says ה׳ of hosts: see if I do not open for you the windows of heaven and pour out for you a blessing until there is more than enough.'
steps.whatsHappening: As with חלה, the teaching ends with the reward: giving מעשרות brings great blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the windows of heaven open, which is the reverse of 'the heavens are held back' in Step 21. The verse even invites us to 'test Me' with this מצוה. The phrase 'עד בלי די' will be explained next.

phrases.english: And if they give, they are blessed,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הָבִיאוּ אֶת כׇּל הַמַּעֲשֵׂר אֶל בֵּית הָאוֹצָר
phrases.english: as it is said: 'Bring all the tithe into the storehouse,'
'so that there will be food in My house,'

phrases.aramaic: וּבְחָנוּנִי נָא בָּזֹאת אָמַר ה׳ צְבָאוֹת
phrases.english: 'and test Me now with this, says ה׳ of hosts,'

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא אֶפְתַּח לָכֶם אֵת אֲרוּבּוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם
phrases.english: 'see if I do not open for you the windows of heaven'

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲרִיקוֹתִי לָכֶם בְּרָכָה עַד בְּלִי דָי״.
phrases.english: 'and pour out for you a blessing until there is more than enough.'
phrases.notes: מלאכי ג:י

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם נוֹתְנִין — מִתְבָּרְכִין, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: הָבִיאוּ אֶת כׇּל הַמַּעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reward side of the תרומות ומעשרות teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those who give מעשרות receive overflowing blessing from heaven.

steps.title: What does 'עד בלי די' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the unusual phrase 'עד בלי די' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'עד בלי די' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about a hard phrase in the verse. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning, 'until there is no more need,' does not seem to add much. The גמרא wants a sharper meaning for these words.

phrases.english: What is 'until more than enough'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a phrase in the verse from Step 24.

steps.title: Your lips will wear out from saying 'enough'
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא, quoting רב, explains: the blessing will be so great that your lips will wear out (יבלו) from saying 'enough' (די).
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said in the name of רב: Until your lips wear out from saying 'Enough!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the phrase and ends this section on a strong note of blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בלי is read as יבלו, 'wear out.' So 'עד בלי די' means you will say 'די' (enough) so many times that your lips get worn out, and the blessing will still keep coming. This ends the section about the reward for giving מעשרות.

keyTerms.meaning: Will wear out (word play on בְּלִי)

steps.whatToRemember: Each sin in this list has a matching punishment. For חלה and מעשרות, the matching reward is also given. The giver of מעשרות is promised blessing 'until your lips wear out from saying enough.'

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said in the name of Rav:
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'בר רב,' but the right reading is 'בר חמא.'

phrases.english: Until your lips wear out from saying 'Enough!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בלי is read as יבלו: the blessing is so great that your lips wear out from saying 'enough.'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Giving מעשרות brings blessing beyond any limit.

steps.title: Robbery brings locusts and terrible famine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that because of the sin of גזל, locusts come, famine spreads, and people end up eating their own children. It brings a פסוק from עמוס about the 'cows of Bashan' who oppress the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the sin of robbery, locusts come up, famine sets in, and people eat the flesh of their sons and daughters. As the פסוק says: 'Hear this word, you cows of Bashan on the mountain of Samaria, who oppress the poor and crush the needy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next sin on its list, גזל, and names its punishment: locusts and a terrible famine. It supports this with a פסוק from עמוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted פסוק names the sin: oppressing and crushing the poor, which is a form of גזל. A few פסוקים later in the same chapter (עמוס ד:ו‎), ה׳ says He gave them 'clean teeth' and 'lack of bread,' which means famine. The lesson is that people who take what belongs to others end up losing their own food.

keyTerms.meaning: Robbery; taking what belongs to someone else
'Cows of Bashan,' a harsh nickname in עמוס for the wealthy who oppress others

steps.confusionAlert: The quoted part of the פסוק only describes the sin (oppressing the poor). It does not mention famine. The famine appears a few פסוקים later in the same chapter (עמוס ד:ו, 'clean teeth' and 'lack of bread'). The גמרא expects you to know the rest of the passage.

phrases.english: Due to the sin of robbery
locusts emerge
and famine prevails
and people eat
the flesh of their sons and daughters
as it is stated
"Hear this word
you cows of Bashan
that are in the mountain of Samaria
that oppress the poor
that crush the needy"
phrases.notes: The famine itself is described later in the passage (עמוס ד:ו).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sin of withholding תרומות ומעשרות (Steps 21–26) to the next sin on the list, גזל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sin of גזל brings locusts, famine, and such desperate hunger that people eat their own children, as derived from עמוס ד.

steps.title: רבא identifies the 'cows of Bashan' with the women of מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: רבא begins to explain who the 'cows of Bashan' are like: the women of the city of מחוזא. His description continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The 'cows of Bashan' are like those women of מחוזא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the picture in the פסוק by comparing the 'cows of Bashan' to the women of his own city, מחוזא. This line only sets up the comparison, and his full explanation of why they are similar comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses a symbolic image, and רבא makes it concrete by pointing to a group of people his listeners knew. מחוזא was a wealthy trading city, so the comparison connects the pampered, well-fed 'cows' to comfortable people who live off others. The details of how they behave are still to come.

keyTerms.meaning: A leading Babylonian אמורא who lived in מחוזא
מחוזא, a wealthy Babylonian city on the Tigris River

phrases.english: Rava said
like those women of Mechoza
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud, where רבא describes their behavior.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כְּגוֹן הָנֵי נְשֵׁי דְמָחוֹזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the phrase 'פרות הבשן' from the פסוק quoted in Step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'cows of Bashan' in the פסוק are like the women of מחוזא. The explanation continues on the next amud.
